lessonRef.title: Performance task planning: judging viable and non-viable options in a modeling context

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: A $40 fee plus $15 per hour totals $115. Write the equation.

steps: Fee is constant; hourly rate multiplies h.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: The formula A = -3bh + 5 models a design constraint, where A, b, and h are positive. Solve it for h.
Item A costs $15 each and item B costs $12 each. You may spend at most $330 in total. Which inequality expresses this constraint on the counts a and b?
A tank holds 290 litres and is filling at 18 litres per minute. After how many minutes does it hold 434 litres?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: A model gives the number of buses needed as 4.3. How should this solution be interpreted?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A repair service charges a $110 call-out fee plus $15 per hour. A job cost $245 in total. Which equation determines the number of hours h?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
